# API stability per C item

`ffimap api` measures a promise a C-to-Rust migration makes to its Rust
consumers: once a C item has a safe Rust API, wrapping it, porting it and its
later stages leave that API alone. It reads the crate's rustdoc JSON, finds the
Rust items that stand in for each C item through their anchors, and records
their consumer-facing surface twice: raw, as the signatures stand, and as the
**contract** a consumer may rely on whatever form a handle or an owner takes.
Two such records, one at the item's first landing and one after a later
landing, say whether the contract was kept, extended or changed. This document is what the two documents hold and every
rule behind them. The scan's counters are [`schema.md`](schema.md)'s and have
nothing to do with it.

## 1. Input

```sh
cargo +nightly-2026-10-07 rustdoc -p CRATE --lib -- -Z unstable-options --output-format json
(cd ffibox && cargo +nightly-2026-10-07 rustdoc --lib -- -Z unstable-options \
    --output-format json --document-private-items)
ffimap api extract target/doc/CRATE.json --dep ffibox/target/doc/ffibox.json > before.json
```

`--dep` gives the rustdoc JSON of a crate the measured one depends on, and is
repeatable. The contracts of handles and owners that are aliases into ffibox
(`CBox`, `CArc`, `CVal`, …) need ffibox's, since the reborrows and trait impls
those forms inherit live there; it is made with `--document-private-items`
because the bounds rustdoc synthesises for ffibox's auto-trait impls name its
private fields' types. Without it those contracts are unresolved, as section 6
describes. The measure is pure Python over the JSON. It does not use the driver, so the
crate need not build on the driver's nightly, only document on one whose JSON
format it reads.

Rustdoc's JSON is unstable: each nightly writes a `format_version`, and the
shape moves with it. `ffimap api` reads **format 61**, which
nightly-2026-10-07 (the driver's pin) and nightly-2026-10-08 emit, and refuses
any other with an error naming the version it found. Support for a new format
is added by checking the fields `src/ffimap/rustdoc.py` reads against it and
adding it to `FORMAT_VERSIONS`.

## 2. C items and their stand-ins

A C item is keyed by its anchor's `<kind>::<path>`: `fn::git_mailmap_new`,
`st::git_mailmap`, `fld::git_buf.ptr`. An anchor is a doc-comment line of its
own, exactly ``Wraps `<kind>::<path>` `` or ``Replaces `<kind>::<path>` ``,
where the path is names separated by dots and a `fld` path names a member. Every
public item of the crate that carries one is a **stand-in** of that C item, and
an item carrying several (the accessor of two members) is a stand-in of each.

What the extract reports about the anchors themselves, under `anchors`:

- `malformed`: a line that tries to be an anchor and is not one -- the verb and
  a `kind::` path inside a sentence, with a trailing period, without backticks,
  or with a path that is not names. It keys nothing.
- `unknown_kinds`: anchors whose kind is not one of the convention's (`fn`,
  `st`, `un`, `enm`, `fnp`, `tdf`, `fld`, `glb`, `mac`), counted by kind. They
  are keyed as written.
- `without_alias`: anchors on an item with no `#[doc(alias)]` naming the
  anchor's path. An item whose own name is the anchor's path is left out:
  rustdoc rejects an alias equal to its item's name, and the name already
  answers a search for it.

## 3. Locators and paths

Each stand-in is named by a **locator**, which is how one landing's record is
matched with the next's:

| item | locator |
|---|---|
| a free item | its canonical path |
| an item of an inherent impl | `Ty::name` |
| an item of a trait impl | `<Ty as Trait<Args>>::name` |
| a trait's item, a variant, a field | its owner's locator `::name` |

Lifetime names in a locator are erased to `'_`.

A **canonical path** is the path a consumer names an item by. For an item of
the crate it is the path rustdoc's `paths` table gives its definition when that
path is public, else the shortest public path it is re-exported at, the first
in order among equals. An item defined in a private module and re-exported from
its parent is named by the parent's path, and a port that moves the definition
into the parent changes nothing. An item of another crate is named by its
definition's path in the `paths` table, `ffibox::refs::CBox` for instance,
because this document does not record that crate's re-exports.

Every type in a signature is rendered by its canonical path, never by what the
source wrote, so an import or a reordering of the source gives the same bytes.

A record's `paths` lists every public path the item is reached by, from the
crate root through public modules and `pub use`, globs included. An associated
item's are its owner's paths with its name appended.

## 4. Signatures

Each stand-in's `sig` is normalised text by kind:

- **functions and methods**: `decl` holds `const`, `async`, `unsafe`, the ABI,
  generics, the receiver (`self`, `&self`, `&'a mut self`, `self: Box<Self>`),
  the parameter types and return type, and where-clauses. A method also has
  the `impl` header it is declared in, generics and trait included, and a
  trait's method has `default`, whether it has a body. Parameter names are
  left out.
- **structs, enums and unions**: `decl` holds the generics, the shape (`;`,
  `(n)`, `{}`) and `#[non_exhaustive]`. `fields` maps each public field to its
  type, and `variants` each variant to its shape and discriminant.
  `stripped` says whether rustdoc hid private fields or variants. `impls` maps
  the header of every trait impl rustdoc records for the type to its items
  (those it defines and the trait's provided ones it inherits) and its
  associated types and constants; the auto-trait impls rustdoc synthesises
  (`Send`, `Sync`, `Unpin`, `UnwindSafe`, `RefUnwindSafe`, and `Freeze` and
  `UnsafeUnpin` where the nightly records them), negative ones as `!Send`, are
  included, and blanket impls are not, since they follow from the type's other
  impls. `members` holds the items of its inherent impls that stand in for no
  C item, each with its impl header.
- **traits**: `decl` with generics, supertraits and `unsafe`; `required` and
  `provided` items, each with its declaration; `dyn_compatible`.
- **type aliases**: `decl` holds the whole target, `type = ffibox::refs::CBox<…>`.
- **constants and statics**: type and value; **associated constants and types**:
  their declaration and, in an impl, its header; **variants** and **fields**:
  their shape or type; a `macro_rules!` macro only its kind, since its body is
  not an interface.

A trait impl's methods are recorded by name only: their signatures are the
trait's, recorded where the trait is.

## 5. Handles and owners

The types a consumer reaches a C type through -- `FooRef`, `FooMut`, `FooBox`,
`FooArc`, `FooVal` and a policy type such as `FooFree` -- are not always
annotated. An unannotated public struct, enum, union or trait of the crate is
**associated** with C items by rule 1, else by rule 2, and a type alias by rule
3; `via` says which rule tied it:

1. `assoc_type`: a trait impl of the type sets an associated type to an
   anchored type, or a trait impl of an anchored type sets one to it.
   `impl CRefSeam for MailmapRef { type Cell = Mailmap; }` and
   `impl CCell for Mailmap { type Ref<'a> = MailmapRef<'a>; }` both tie
   `MailmapRef` to `st::git_mailmap`.
2. `owner`: the type's impls, or the trait's declaration, hold stand-ins; it is
   associated with their C items. A policy type whose `CDrop::c_drop` wraps
   `fn::git_mailmap_free` goes with that item.
3. `alias`: a type alias whose target names an anchored type, by id anywhere in
   the target, goes with that type's C items: `MailmapBox = CBox<Mailmap,
   MailmapFree>` with `st::git_mailmap`. A target naming none goes with the
   items of the types it names that rules 1 and 2 associated.

An associated item is recorded under each of its C items with the record a
stand-in has, and a C item's surface is its stand-ins and its associated items
together.

## 6. The contract view

A handle or an owner changes form over a migration: `FooRef` is a pointer
wrapper while `Foo` is wrapped and `&'a Foo` once it is ported, `FooBox` an
ffibox `CBox` and then a `Box`. A consumer relies only on what every form
offers, as `binding-types` states: their methods, their reborrows (`as_ref`,
`as_mut`) and the dereferences the native forms offer. The **contract** of a
type is that, and it, not the raw record, decides a C item's status.

Every C item has a `contract` view: one entry per stand-in or associated item.

- **A type** (`Foo`, `FooRef`, `FooMut`, `FooBox`, `FooArc`, `FooVal`, a
  policy type, an enum) has its contract under its locator:
  - `generics`: how many lifetimes, types and constants it takes;
  - `fields` (public ones), `shape` (only when a consumer can build it, no
    field hidden), `variants` and `non_exhaustive`;
  - `methods`: every method a consumer can call on it, by name, over every
    route: on the form itself, through its dereferences (`&self` methods
    through `Deref`, `&mut self` ones too through `DerefMut`) and on what its
    reborrows return. The route is not recorded, and the first found names a
    method;
  - `reborrows`: what `as_ref` and `as_mut` return. One returning the form's
    own type adds nothing and is left out;
  - `traits`: the traits it implements that a consumer can use, with their
    arguments;
  - `derefs`: targets reached through a dereference that the contract does
    not look inside (a slice, `str`, a primitive, a standard type), whose
    methods are the standard library's.
- **A method of a handle or owner** is keyed `method::<name>`, without its
  owner, since a port moves it from `FooRef` to `impl Foo`, and holds its
  normalised signatures.
- **Any other function** has its normalised signature; anything else its raw
  record.

Signatures in a contract are normalised so that each form reads the same: a
type equal to the target of one of the crate's public aliases is written as the
alias, so `&'a Foo` reads `FooRef<'_>` once `FooRef<'a> = &'a Foo`; lifetimes
are erased; `Self` is the type the method is called on; a projection such as
`<Foo as CCell>::Ref<'_>` is resolved through `Foo`'s impl; parameter names
are dropped; and a `self` receiver of a `Copy` type is `&self`.

**What is no part of a contract:**

| left out | why |
|---|---|
| functions without a `self` receiver | reached through a type path, which a change of form changes |
| the seams `as_ptr`, `as_mut_ptr`, `as_void_ptr`, `from_ptr`, `from_void_ptr`, `from_raw_parts`, `into_raw_parts`, `from_c`, `into_c`, `as_c_ptr`, `from_raw`, `as_object` | the conversion between a wrapper and its raw form, ffimap's seam list |
| a method with a raw pointer or `NonNull` in its signature | raw access |
| `unsafe` methods | they exist because a form wraps C; an anchored one is its own C item's |
| anchored methods | each is its own C item's stand-in, compared there |
| every method of a plumbing crate's type (`--plumbing`, ffibox by default) but `as_ref` and `as_mut` | what one form offers beyond the native ones, such as `try_clone` or `policy` |

## 3. Locators and paths

Each stand-in is named by a **locator**, which is how one landing's record is
matched with the next's:

| item | locator |
|---|---|
| a free item | its canonical path |
| an item of an inherent impl | `Ty::name` |
| an item of a trait impl | `<Ty as Trait<Args>>::name` |
| a trait's item, a variant, a field | its owner's locator `::name` |

Lifetime names in a locator are erased to `'_`.

A **canonical path** is the path a consumer names an item by. For an item of
the crate it is the path rustdoc's `paths` table gives its definition when that
path is public, else the shortest public path it is re-exported at, the first
in order among equals. An item defined in a private module and re-exported from
its parent is named by the parent's path, and a port that moves the definition
into the parent changes nothing. An item of another crate is named by its
definition's path in the `paths` table, `ffibox::refs::CBox` for instance,
because this document does not record that crate's re-exports.

Every type in a signature is rendered by its canonical path, never by what the
source wrote, so an import or a reordering of the source gives the same bytes.

A record's `paths` lists every public path the item is reached by, from the
crate root through public modules and `pub use`, globs included. An associated
item's are its owner's paths with its name appended.

## 4. Signatures

Each stand-in's `sig` is normalised text by kind:

- **functions and methods**: `decl` holds `const`, `async`, `unsafe`, the ABI,
  generics, the receiver (`self`, `&self`, `&'a mut self`, `self: Box<Self>`),
  the parameter types and return type, and where-clauses. A method also has
  the `impl` header it is declared in, generics and trait included, and a
  trait's method has `default`, whether it has a body. Parameter names are
  left out.
- **structs, enums and unions**: `decl` holds the generics, the shape (`;`,
  `(n)`, `{}`) and `#[non_exhaustive]`. `fields` maps each public field to its
  type, and `variants` each variant to its shape and discriminant.
  `stripped` says whether rustdoc hid private fields or variants. `impls` maps
  the header of every trait impl rustdoc records for the type to its items
  (those it defines and the trait's provided ones it inherits) and its
  associated types and constants; the auto-trait impls rustdoc synthesises
  (`Send`, `Sync`, `Unpin`, `UnwindSafe`, `RefUnwindSafe`, and `Freeze` and
  `UnsafeUnpin` where the nightly records them), negative ones as `!Send`, are
  included, and blanket impls are not, since they follow from the type's other
  impls. `members` holds the items of its inherent impls that stand in for no
  C item, each with its impl header.
- **traits**: `decl` with generics, supertraits and `unsafe`; `required` and
  `provided` items, each with its declaration; `dyn_compatible`.
- **type aliases**: `decl` holds the whole target, `type = ffibox::refs::CBox<…>`.
- **constants and statics**: type and value; **associated constants and types**:
  their declaration and, in an impl, its header; **variants** and **fields**:
  their shape or type; a `macro_rules!` macro only its kind, since its body is
  not an interface.

A trait impl's methods are recorded by name only: their signatures are the
trait's, recorded where the trait is.

## 5. Handles and owners

The types a consumer reaches a C type through -- `FooRef`, `FooMut`, `FooBox`,
`FooArc`, `FooVal` and a policy type such as `FooFree` -- are not always
annotated. An unannotated public struct, enum, union or trait of the crate is
**associated** with C items by rule 1, else by rule 2, and a type alias by rule
3; `via` says which rule tied it:

1. `assoc_type`: a trait impl of the type sets an associated type to an
   anchored type, or a trait impl of an anchored type sets one to it.
   `impl CRefSeam for MailmapRef { type Cell = Mailmap; }` and
   `impl CCell for Mailmap { type Ref<'a> = MailmapRef<'a>; }` both tie
   `MailmapRef` to `st::git_mailmap`.
2. `owner`: the type's impls, or the trait's declaration, hold stand-ins; it is
   associated with their C items. A policy type whose `CDrop::c_drop` wraps
   `fn::git_mailmap_free` goes with that item.
3. `alias`: a type alias whose target names an anchored type, by id anywhere in
   the target, goes with that type's C items: `MailmapBox = CBox<Mailmap,
   MailmapFree>` with `st::git_mailmap`. A target naming none goes with the
   items of the types it names that rules 1 and 2 associated.

An associated item is recorded under each of its C items with the record a
stand-in has, and a C item's surface is its stand-ins and its associated items
together.

## 6. The contract view

A handle or an owner changes form over a migration: `FooRef` is a pointer
wrapper while `Foo` is wrapped and `&'a Foo` once it is ported, `FooBox` an
ffibox `CBox` and then a `Box`. A consumer relies only on what every form
offers, as `binding-types` states: their methods, their reborrows (`as_ref`,
`as_mut`) and the dereferences the native forms offer. The **contract** of a
type is that, and it, not the raw record, decides a C item's status.

Every C item has a `contract` view: one entry per stand-in or associated item.

- **A type** (`Foo`, `FooRef`, `FooMut`, `FooBox`, `FooArc`, `FooVal`, a
  policy type, an enum) has its contract under its locator:
  - `generics`: how many lifetimes, types and constants it takes;
  - `fields` (public ones), `shape` (only when a consumer can build it, no
    field hidden), `variants` and `non_exhaustive`;
  - `methods`: every method a consumer can call on it, by name, over every
    route: on the form itself, through its dereferences (`&self` methods
    through `Deref`, `&mut self` ones too through `DerefMut`) and on what its
    reborrows return. The route is not recorded, and the first found names a
    method;
  - `reborrows`: what `as_ref` and `as_mut` return. One returning the form's
    own type adds nothing and is left out;
  - `traits`: the traits it implements that a consumer can use, with their
    arguments;
  - `derefs`: targets reached through a dereference that the contract does
    not look inside (a slice, `str`, a primitive, a standard type), whose
    methods are the standard library's.
- **A method of a handle or owner** is keyed `method::<name>`, without its
  owner, since a port moves it from `FooRef` to `impl Foo`, and holds its
  normalised signatures.
- **Any other function** has its normalised signature; anything else its raw
  record.

Signatures in a contract are normalised so that each form reads the same: a
type equal to the target of one of the crate's public aliases is written as the
alias, so `&'a Foo` reads `FooRef<'_>` once `FooRef<'a> = &'a Foo`; lifetimes
are erased; `Self` is the type the method is called on; a projection such as
`<Foo as CCell>::Ref<'_>` is resolved through `Foo`'s impl; parameter names
are dropped; and a `self` receiver of a `Copy` type is `&self`.

**What is no part of a contract:**

| left out | why |
|---|---|
| functions without a `self` receiver | reached through a type path, which a change of form changes |
| the seams `as_ptr`, `as_mut_ptr`, `as_void_ptr`, `from_ptr`, `from_void_ptr`, `from_raw_parts`, `into_raw_parts`, `from_c`, `into_c`, `as_c_ptr`, `from_raw`, `as_object` | the conversion between a wrapper and its raw form, ffimap's seam list |
| a method with a raw pointer or `NonNull` in its signature | raw access |
| `unsafe` methods | they exist because a form wraps C; an anchored one is its own C item's |
| anchored methods | each is its own C item's stand-in, compared there |
| every method of a plumbing crate's type (`--plumbing`, ffibox by default) but `as_ref` and `as_mut` | what one form offers beyond the native ones, such as `try_clone` or `policy` |

### `libgit2/src/util/cc-compat.h` wave 219 batch 0: the module's `port`

The module's whole `port`, five macros, in `src/libgit2/src/util/cc_compat_h.rs`, which holds
no unsafe region and carries `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`. `src/util/cc-compat.h` has no
translation unit. No C reaches the port, so no macro has an export. Each macro stays in the
header for the C that expands it, which keeps it past the ship point: `GIT_UNUSED` in 338
functions, `PRIdZ`, `PRIuZ` and `PRIxZ` in 26 TUs under `src/`, `clar_libgit2.c` and 54 test
files, and `va_copy` in `str.c`'s `git_str_vprintf`. The module's docs list them, and the
header's definitions no module owns. Each item is the branch this build takes: clang at
`-std=c90` (`__GNUC__`, neither MSVC nor MinGW). There `<stdarg.h>` defines `__va_copy` but not
`va_copy`, so the header defines `va_copy` as `__va_copy`, that is `__builtin_va_copy`. Each
item's docs name the branches not taken, which compute the same:

- `mac::GIT_UNUSED` is `const fn unused<T: ?Sized>(_: &T)`, Rust's `let _ = &x;`. It takes
  its argument by reference, so it neither moves nor drops it, whatever its type.
- `mac::PRIdZ`, `mac::PRIuZ` and `mac::PRIxZ` are the `&str` constants `PRI_DZ`, `PRI_UZ`
  and `PRI_XZ` (`"zd"`, `"zu"`, `"zx"`), for C format strings built in Rust. Their docs name
  Rust's `{}` and `{:x}` as the native equivalent, as `modules.json`'s `rust_equivalent` has
  it.
- `mac::va_copy` is `const fn va_copy(&fmt::Arguments) -> fmt::Arguments`, a copy. Rust
  formats `fmt::Arguments` where C formats a `va_list`, and formatting does not consume it.
  `core::ffi::VaList`'s `Clone` is unstable (`c_variadic`). The function has no alias, since
  its name is the C name.

The raw bindings gain `var PRIdZ|PRIuZ|PRIxZ` (`b"zd\0"` and the others), against which the
equivalence tests compare the constants. The `loc` cell is wavefront's `0` for macros.

Tests: eight `unit_pub` tests, two doctests and four `equiv` tests. The unit tests check
`unused`'s move, drop and type cases and its `const` use, the formats' values and the C

### `libgit2/src/util/cc-compat.h` wave 219 batch 1: module pass

The module pass, and the module's only review, over batch 0's three paths (`f570d2a4e`), for
every objective with `fix`. It files one finding, `misc/size-formats-ported-with-one-branch`
(`nit`), and fixes it. The header's `PRIdZ`, `PRIuZ` and `PRIxZ` name Microsoft's `I64` and
`I` modifiers under `_MSC_VER` or `__MINGW32__`, and C99's `z` elsewhere. Batch 0 gave the
Rust constants this build's `"zd"`, `"zu"` and `"zx"` for every target. `porting-symbols`
ports a macro once only where every configured branch computes the same result, and these
strings differ. Rust's `cfg` sees the header's conditions. `clang --target=<t> -E` of the
header gives `"I64d"` and `"Id"` on 64- and 32-bit `pc-windows-msvc` and `w64-mingw32`. A
scratch `no_std` check of the module's constants fails on `x86_64-pc-windows-gnu` at the tip.
The fix, a local `size_format!`, defines each constant once per branch under its `cfg`, from
one invocation holding its docs, anchor and alias. The check passes on the five Windows and
Linux targets tried, and this build's values and rustdoc are unchanged. The crate builds for
Linux alone, so no consumer observed it.

The rest holds. `unused` evaluates its argument once and neither moves nor drops it, as both
branches of `GIT_UNUSED` do. `va_copy` over `fmt::Arguments` is what a Rust consumer of
`git_str_vprintf`'s port needs. `fmt::Arguments` is `Copy`, formatting does not consume it,
and `VaList` is unstable. Its three branches (the builtin, the C library's and the assignment)
all give a copy, verified for this build by preprocessing `str.c`'s flags (`-std=c90`:
`__builtin_va_copy`). Anchors, aliases (none on `va_copy`, whose name is the C name), the
header-module home, `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]` and the tests' placement in `unit_pub` follow
the conventions. The three allowlisted constants serve the equivalence test against the
header's expansion, and stay valid while the header does. No equivalence test of `GIT_UNUSED`
is right as `crustify/evolution/equiv-macro-without-effect` argues: no expansion site passes
an argument with an effect, and the function holding it behaves the same without it. The
provisional lessons `cmake-property-naming-a-removed-source` and
`http-exports-gated-through-a-local-remote` are marked `held`. Their evidence was checked
against the fork's `deps/llhttp/CMakeLists.txt`, gen5's `build.ninja`, a scratch CMake project
(a property naming missing sources configures, and an empty glob fails with "can not determine
linker language"), `http-gate.sh`'s four failing clones and both switches'
`http-gate-results.txt`.

Gates ran as `end-gates` snapshots under the worktree's `crustify/tmp/`, at 24 jobs (20 for the
landed tree), with the slow list's skips. On the wave tip `f570d2a4e`, `fmt --check` and
`clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings` pass, with no export feature to lint. Plain,
ASan+UBSan and TSan pass the workspace: `lib` 907 and 1 ignored, `equiv` 536, `hidden_symbols`
1, `ub_safe` 798, `ub_unsafe` 144, `unit_pub` 249, doctests 108 and 397. Miri passes every
binary: `lib` 447, `ub_safe` 213, `unit_pub` 163, `equiv` 39 and `ub_unsafe` 26 passed, the
rest marked. BSan passes every binary, each under a 3,600 s timeout: `lib` 903, `ub_safe` 767,
`ub_unsafe` 144, `unit_pub` 248, `equiv` 452 (1,850 s), `hidden_symbols` 1. On the landed tree
(`b1a50b046`'s tree), the lint, plain, ASan+UBSan, TSan and Miri runs give the tip's counts.
BSan was rerun on the four `equiv` tests of the module, each alone by exact name, and on
`unit_pub`, all passing. BSan's other binaries keep the tip's results. The fix changes three
constants whose values on this target are the tip's literals, and no test or other code.

The safety audit scan (ffimap `50a800e`, flags as batch 0's) differs from batch 0's only in
`code.loc.total` (`+10`), which moves the Overview's Rust LoC and `unsafe loc %`. Its boundary
sites hold none in the module. `ffimap api` against the tip (nightly `2026-10-08`, ffibox's
private rustdoc JSON) keeps the five items and every unattributed module. A first form of
the fix, a `cfg!`-selected table, read as `changed`, since rustdoc renders a non-literal value
as `_`. Coverage was not measured again: the change adds no test and no runtime code. No raw
binding or C changed, so the packaging gate does not apply. Usage cells are the assistant's.

Proposal: `config-branches-rust-cfg` (`porting-symbols`' Macros section). It routes a macro
whose branches differ under conditions Rust's `cfg` tests to one item per branch, and it cites
the watched row `config-branches-of-one-result`.

Rust constants this build's `"zd"`, `"zu"` and `"zx"` for every target. `porting-symbols`
ports a macro once only where every configured branch computes the same result, and these
strings differ. Rust's `cfg` sees the header's conditions. `clang --target=<t> -E` of the
header gives `"I64d"` and `"Id"` on 64- and 32-bit `pc-windows-msvc` and `w64-mingw32`. A
scratch `no_std` check of the module's constants fails on `x86_64-pc-windows-gnu` at the tip.

one invocation holding its docs, anchor and alias. The check passes on the five Windows and
Linux targets tried, and this build's values and rustdoc are unchanged. The crate builds for
Linux alone, so no consumer observed it.

branches of `GIT_UNUSED` do. `va_copy` over `fmt::Arguments` is what a Rust consumer of

header's expansion, and stay valid while the header does. No equivalence test of `GIT_UNUSED`

content.text:
I finished the module pass of `src/util/cc-compat.h` and landed it on `crustify/waves/wave-219` as `9b4c4b07c` (the reviews commit) and `ae2005148` (the fix, dashboard and run dir). It found one defect, now fixed, and filed one proposal.

**Finding, fixed: `misc/size-formats-ported-with-one-branch` (`nit`).**
- **Defect:** `PRI_DZ`, `PRI_UZ` and `PRI_XZ` held this build's `"zd"`, `"zu"` and `"zx"` for every target. The header gives `"I64d"` on 64-bit Windows and `"Id"` on 32-bit Windows, for both MSVC and MinGW; I confirmed this by preprocessing the header for each target with `clang -E`. `porting-symbols` ports a macro once only when every branch computes the same result, and these strings differ.
- **Exception doesn't apply:** the shim is for a configuration Rust can't see, and Rust's `cfg` sees these conditions (`windows`, `target_pointer_width`).
- **Fix:** a local `size_format!` macro defines each constant once per header branch under its `cfg`. The docs, anchor and alias are written once per constant. A scratch check of the constants fails on `x86_64-pc-windows-gnu` before the fix and passes on five Windows and Linux targets after it.
- **Effect here:** none. The crate only builds for Linux, so no consumer could see the difference. On this build the values and rustdoc are unchanged, and `ffimap api` keeps all five items. My first version, a lookup table, showed up as `changed`, because rustdoc renders its values as `_`.

**The rest of the port holds:**
- **`va_copy` over `fmt::Arguments`** is what a Rust consumer of `git_str_vprintf`'s port needs. `fmt::Arguments` is `Copy` and formatting doesn't consume it, while `VaList` is unstable. All three header branches produce a copy; on this build it is `__builtin_va_copy` at `-std=c90`, which I checked by preprocessing with the build's flags.
- **`unused`** is correct: it evaluates its argument once and neither moves nor drops it.
- **Allowlist:** the three allowlisted constants are needed for the equivalence test against the header's expansion. They stay valid while the header stays in `c/`. The integration should decide whether those tests and allowlist entries stay after the switch.
- **No equivalence test for `GIT_UNUSED`** is right, as `equiv-macro-without-effect` argues. That proposal is not in `INDEX.md` yet, which is for the assistant to add.

**Lessons:** I marked `cmake-property-naming-a-removed-source` and `http-exports-gated-through-a-local-remote` as `held`. I checked both against the fork's `deps/llhttp/CMakeLists.txt`, gen5's `build.ninja`, a scratch CMake project, `http-gate.sh` and the two switches' recorded results.

**Gates:**
- **Tip `f570d2a4e`:** formatting, clippy, plain, ASan+UBSan, TSan, Miri and BSan all pass on every binary, with the slow list skipped. BSan `equiv` took 1,850 s.
- **Landed tree:** lint, plain, ASan+UBSan, TSan and Miri give the tip's exact counts. BSan passes the module's four `equiv` tests, each run alone. It passed all 248 `unit_pub` tests that finished; I stopped the slow-list test `decode_char_reads_every_char` after a minute, since the end gates skip it.
- **After the rebase I reran nothing:** the wave tip was still my base, so the landing was a plain fast-forward with nothing new combined in.
- **Why the rest of BSan stands:** I didn't rerun BSan's other binaries on the fix, because on Linux the fix compiles the same three literal strings as before and changes no test or other code.

**Dashboard:** I filled my landing cells only: rows in the tests, safety audit and API stability tables and in both Module passes tables, the affected Σ cells, the Overview's Rust LoC (+10) and a Notes entry. I didn't measure coverage again, since the fix adds no test and no runtime code.

**Proposal:** I filed `crustify/evolution/config-branches-rust-cfg` against `porting-symbols`' Macros section. When a macro's branches differ under conditions Rust's `cfg` can test, the spec currently gives no route; the proposal ports one item per branch under its `cfg`. It cites the watched row `config-branches-of-one-result`.

I deleted the scratch builds (about 12 GB) and kept the logs in `crustify/tmp/`.
